title: Fynaptix · Space Economy Research
heading: Space Economy Intelligence
subheading: Launch, satellites, constellations & the post-SpaceX-IPO landscape
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Space is capital-intensive with heavy government-customer concentration. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Global space economy estimated at ~$626B in 2026 and projected to reach $1.8T by 2035; private space-startup funding was last reported at a record $20.3B year to date.

SpaceX closed at $160.57 on Oct 8 (-4.2% that day, ~+1% on the week through Thursday and the only listed space name up); 52-week range $104.83-$225.64, consensus average target ~$208 (range $115-$280).
Up to 328.4M shares became eligible for sale on Friday under the staggered post-IPO lockup; a further, larger tranche follows Q3 earnings (date not yet confirmed).

RKLB fell ~8% (about $68-71) as Neutron's 13,000 kg payload was compared with Falcon 9's 17,000 kg and Peter Beck said the window for a flight before year-end is narrowing; ASTS -3%, RDW -10%, PL -2% over the same period.

tiers.label: Scale Players
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Agreed to buy Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio (WSJ: ~$8B cash, subject to FCC approval); the FCC approved Starlink Mobile Gen2 for 15,000 satellites and American Airlines plans Starlink across 1,000+ mainline aircraft from early 2027. Starlink last reported 12.0M subscribers; shares closed $160.57 on Oct 8 (~$2.12T).
rows.watch for: Staggered lockup supply (up to 328.4M shares eligible Oct 9, more after Q3 earnings), falling Starlink ARPU ($66 vs $85), $23.6B of H1 AI capex and the ~$8B spectrum outlay.

rows.angle: Fell ~8% on the week to ~$68-71 despite constructive ARK commentary; signed 20 more Synspective Electron launches (2028-2031, 47 contracted in total). $8B Iridium deal fully funded by the $1.94B at-the-market sale; close still guided to mid-2027.
rows.watch for: Neutron (13,000 kg vs Falcon 9's 17,000 kg) with Beck saying the pre-year-end window is narrowing, FCC review of Iridium, and a valuation above 40x annualized revenue on a $49.3M Q2 net loss.

rows.angle: No new space award this week; backlog still anchored by the $955M share of the SDA's $1.75B Golden Dome tracking-layer award (36 satellites in total, 18 of them L3Harris) and the $4.7B PAC-3 propulsion award; also in the Defense sleeve.
rows.watch for: Conversion of awards into margin, with launches of this batch not expected until 2028; don't double-count with the Defense sleeve.

tiers.label: Growth / Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Completed its first Telus network integration test (Telus expects customer availability within a year) and a US-Japan statement welcomed its Rakuten cooperation; BlueBirds 14-16 are at Cape Canaveral. Shares -3% on the week and ~-22% YTD.
rows.watch for: SpaceX's Grain spectrum deal and Starlink Mobile Gen2 approval raise direct-to-device competition (ASTS fell ~4% after hours Thursday), on top of B.Riley's Neutral and $65 target and rivals Viasat and Space42's Equatys.

rows.angle: Fell ~7% to ~$14 on Oct 7 in a sector-wide sell-off; still reports a record $1.8B backlog and recently took an order for two modular satellite platforms from an undisclosed customer.
rows.watch for: Net insider selling of roughly $259M over 12 months, lunar missions' dependence on government timing, and whether the backlog converts to recognized revenue.

rows.angle: Part of Google's Project Suncatcher prototype (launched Oct 1; Google confirmed contact and normal operation, with TPU testing over the next few weeks); Barclays initiated at Equal Weight with a $17 target. Shares -2% on the week, ~-13% YTD.
rows.watch for: Barclays' target implies ~1% downside from current levels, dependence on SpaceX rideshare capacity (which tightens by 2028), and founder stock sales.

rows.angle: Awarded two Roll-Out Solar Array wings for Axiom Space's second station module (first module launches 2028); one of 15 NITE STAR vendors. Fell ~10% on the week to ~$9.6-10.1, ~-28% YTD.
rows.watch for: NITE STAR carries no guaranteed revenue, Axiom's timelines are years out, and the $1.15B of net insider selling over 12 months remains unexplained.

private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: New Glenn exploded during a static hot fire at LC-36 on May 28, destroying the transporter-erector at its only pad; CEO Dave Limp is still targeting another launch before the end of 2026, which looks ambitious for the repair work involved. Reports (not verified here) say Blue Origin is seeking ~$10B at a ~$130B valuation.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: No fresh news found this week beyond the Starcloud lunar AI-computing deal and the Sept 22 cleanroom opening; Alpha Block 2's debut remains slated for Q4 2026.

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: No fresh update this week beyond the $1B Series E (total raised $2.3B, ~$10B valuation); Nova Block 2, a 15-metric-ton fully reusable design, is still targeted for 2029.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: Rocket Lab raised $1.94B of equity (~$66 a share) on a $49.3M quarterly net loss and could reach ~12% dilution after the Iridium close; AST SpaceMobile carries a $1.15B convertible plus ~$610M of quarterly capex; SpaceX spent $23.6B on AI capex in H1 and now adds a reported ~$8B spectrum purchase.

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: The SDA's $1.75B Tranche 3 award was split between L3Harris ($955M) and Sierra Space ($798M), NITE-STAR is a pooled vehicle with no guaranteed revenue, and Axiom-type commercial-station work is years from launch; Golden Dome spending is large but spread thin.

bear_case.title: SpaceX absorbs the value / lockups
bear_case.description: At ~$2.1T SpaceX is priced for flawless execution, Starlink ARPU is falling, 328.4M more shares became eligible Oct 9 with a larger tranche after Q3 earnings, and its spectrum buys now push it directly at AST SpaceMobile's direct-to-device market.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk
bear_case.description: Neutron's maiden launch is slipping towards 2027 (payload 13,000 kg vs Falcon 9's 17,000 kg), Flight 14 still lost an engine on ascent, Blue Origin's only pad was wrecked in May, and a failure in any of these resets sector sentiment quickly; the Oct 7 sell-off hit RKLB, LUNR and RDW together on no company news.

catalysts.title: SpaceX lockup tranche of up to 328.4M shares
catalysts.description: Eligible for sale Friday under the staggered post-IPO lockup; SPCX closed $160.57 on Oct 8 and ended the week roughly +1% as the only listed space name in the green.

catalysts.title: SpaceX buys spectrum; FCC approves Starlink Mobile Gen2
catalysts.description: Agreed to acquire Grain Management's 800 MHz portfolio (WSJ: ~$8B cash, subject to FCC approval) and won FCC approval for 15,000 Gen2 satellites; American Airlines will fit Starlink across 1,000+ aircraft from early 2027. AST SpaceMobile slipped ~4% after hours on the competitive read-through.

catalysts.title: Space stocks sell off together
catalysts.description: LUNR -7% (~$14.07), RKLB -5% (~$71) and RDW -5% (~$10.09) on no company-specific news while the S&P 500 was flat; UFO -3% to ~$42.86.

catalysts.title: Rocket Lab -8% on Neutron questions
catalysts.description: ARK said Neutron 'comes close to the Falcon 9' but is a little shy on payload; Beck said the window for a 2026 flight is narrowing. Offsetting: 20 more Synspective Electron launches (47 contracted).

catalysts.title: Telus-AST integration test; Axiom awards Redwire
catalysts.description: AST and Telus completed their first network integration test; Axiom Space awarded Redwire two Roll-Out Solar Array wings for its second station module.

catalysts.title: SpaceX Q3 earnings and next lockup release
catalysts.description: Date not yet confirmed; a larger block of shares follows the release. Blue Origin still targets New Glenn's return to flight before year-end, and Neutron delivery to the pad is guided for Q4 2026.

etfs.name: Procure Space
etfs.summary: Pure-play, revenue-weighted (RKLB, PL, ASTS among top holdings); ~$42.86 on Oct 7 after a 3% drop; up roughly 23% over the trailing 12 months as last reported Sept 28.

etfs.name: ARK Space Exploration
etfs.summary: Actively managed with broader tech adjacency; up roughly 18% trailing 12 months as last reported, and ARK has been adding RKLB.

etfs.name: SPDR Kensho Final Frontiers
etfs.summary: Equal-weight space, defense and deep-sea blend; up roughly 42% trailing 12 months as last reported, the strongest of the three.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rocket Lab
positions.note: Fell ~8% on the week to ~$68-71 as Neutron's 13,000 kg payload (vs Falcon 9's 17,000 kg) and Beck's warning that the 2026 flight window is narrowing sank in, though 20 more Synspective launches (47 contracted) and a funded $8B Iridium deal keep the revenue thesis intact; at 40x+ annualized revenue the weight is trimmed to 30.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: Holds the $955M share of the SDA's $1.75B Golden Dome tracking award and the $4.7B PAC-3 propulsion award with no negative news this week, so it carries the most weight as the sector's funded-backlog name; also sits in the Defense sleeve, so don't double-count it.

positions.name: AST SpaceMobile
positions.note: Telus integration test was a real step, but SpaceX's ~$8B Grain spectrum deal and Starlink Mobile Gen2 approval sharpen the direct-to-device threat (shares -3% on the week, ~-22% YTD, B.Riley at Neutral with a $65 target), so the weight is trimmed again.

positions.name: Intuitive Machines
positions.note: Dropped ~7% to ~$14 in the Oct 7 sector sell-off with no company news; the $1.8B backlog and new two-platform satellite order are real, but ~$259M of net insider selling over 12 months and unproven conversion keep it small.

positions.name: Planet Labs
positions.note: Google's Suncatcher prototype is operating as expected and Planet is a named partner, but Barclays' Equal Weight and $17 target imply ~1% downside, so it stays small and speculative.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: The only space name up on the week (+1%; $160.57 on Oct 8, ~$2.12T) with an ~$8B spectrum purchase, Starlink Mobile Gen2 approval and an American Airlines deal, but 328.4M lockup shares unlocked Oct 9, more follow Q3 earnings, and ARPU is falling, so it stays on Watch; UK investors wanting indirect exposure can use Scottish Mortgage (SMT, covered on the Baillie Gifford page).

positions.name: Redwire
positions.note: Fell ~10% on the week (~$9.6-10.1, ~-28% YTD) despite the Axiom solar-array award; the NITE STAR slot carries no guaranteed revenue and $1.15B of net insider selling over 12 months is still unexplained, so it stays out of the sleeve.

positions.name: Iridium Communications
positions.note: Shareholders already approved the Rocket Lab deal (99.6% of votes), leaving only FCC review before a mid-2027 close, so the standalone stock is just a spread on RKLB's share price and RKLB is the cleaner way to hold the view.
